title: Fastify Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Return a greeting
examples.description: A Fastify handler can return a value directly. Open GET /.

examples.title: Return an object
examples.description: Fastify turns a returned object into JSON. Open GET /book.

examples.title: Read a route input
examples.description: A colon marks a path parameter. GET /hello/Ravi puts the name in request.params.

examples.title: Read a query string
examples.description: Query input follows the question mark. GET /search?q=cat reads q.

examples.title: Read a JSON body
examples.description: Fastify can parse JSON bodies. Send POST /books with application/json and {"title":"Moon Trip"}.

examples.title: Validate a path value
examples.description: A schema describes allowed data. GET /books/3 converts and checks id as a positive integer.

examples.title: Run a step before a handler
examples.description: A preHandler hook runs before the route handler. GET / uses the request field set by the hook.

examples.title: Share a helper
examples.description: decorate adds a named helper to the Fastify instance. GET / uses that helper.

examples.title: Group routes in a plugin
examples.description: register gives a plugin its own scope. A prefix puts its routes under /api. Open GET /api/books.

examples.title: Choose response fields
examples.description: A response schema can choose which fields are sent. GET /book keeps title and leaves out internalNote.

examples.title: Give a clear error reply
examples.description: setErrorHandler handles errors from routes. GET /broken returns a simple public message.

examples.title: Test without an open port
examples.description: inject runs a request inside Fastify. This example prints the response body and closes the app without listening.
